question: Pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 20, 30 and 60 hours, respectively. Pipes A, B and C are opened at 7 a.m., 8 a.m., and 9 a.m., respectively, on the same day. When will the tank be full?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 20, 30, 60) = 60 units. Efficiency: A = 3, B = 2, C = 1.

Work done by A (7 am to 9 am) = 3 × 2 = 6 units.

Work done by B (8 am to 9 am) = 2 × 1 = 2 units.

Remaining work at 9 am = 60 − (6 + 2) = 52 units.

Time after 9 am = 52 ÷ (3 + 2 + 1) = 52 ÷ 6 = 8 hours 40 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 40 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Pipe A fills in 20 hrs, B in 30 hrs, C in 60 hrs. Start times: A at 7 a.m., B at 8 a.m., C at 9 a.m.

⇒ Work done by A till 9 a.m. (2 hours) = 3 × 2 = 6 units

⇒ Work done by B till 9 a.m. (1 hour) = 2 × 1 = 2 units

⇒ Total work completed till 9 a.m. = 6 + 2 = 8 units

⇒ Remaining work to be filled = 60 − 8 = 52 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B, and C = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units/hour

⇒ Time required after 9 a.m. = 52 ÷ 6 = 8 hours 40 minutes

⇒ Final filling time = 9:00 a.m. + 8 hours 40 minutes = 5:40 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 40 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

If an inlet pipe fills in X hours and an outlet pipe empties in Y hours, the net work in 1 hour is (1/X − 1/Y).

Fraction to Time Conversion

To convert hours in fraction to minutes, multiply the fraction part by 60. E.g., 2/3 hours = 2/3 × 60 = 40 minutes.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple pipes operate together, their efficiencies are additive. Total time = Total Work ÷ Sum of individual efficiencies.</p
